rows.title: Coalition to back CT officials willing to work around spending cap
rows.standfirst: The group vows to help CT legislators work around the spending cap. Meanwhile, a progressive caucus is renewing its fight for tax fairness.

rows.title: CT remains on pace for big surplus, but revenue begins to slow
rows.standfirst: CT will see the second-largest budget surplus in its history, but investment-related income tax receipts have begun to pull back.

rows.title: House GOP budget plan ups the ante on CT tax-cutting proposals
rows.standfirst: CT House Republicans unveiled a $50.7 billion budget plan for the next two fiscal years, centered on $700 million per year in tax relief.

rows.title: CT Senate GOP budget plan calls for $750M in annual tax relief
rows.standfirst: The CT Senate Republicans’ proposal is centered on an income tax cut and relies heavily on freezing vacant positions across state government.

rows.title: New CT debt report offers sobering look at state finances
rows.standfirst: An analysis shows CT’s health care program for retired state workers, by one metric, was the fifth-worst funded among all states in 2019.

rows.title: Next CT budget will hinge on Lamont’s ability to find big savings
rows.standfirst: A bipartisan deal on a CT budget, including the first income tax rate cut in decades, could come by the end of the week, leaders said.

rows.title: ‘Baby Bonds’ for youths in poverty salvaged after compromise
rows.standfirst: CT’s Baby Bonds program could launch in July after Treasurer Erick Russell and Gov. Ned Lamont reached deal to avoid millions in interest.

rows.title: Union to strike at group homes serving 1,500 disabled clients
rows.standfirst: More than 1,700 members of SEIU 1199NE seeking a ‘pathway to $25/hour’ are set to strike May 24 against six agencies that run group homes.

rows.title: CT budget deal approaches, but the bottom line is blurry
rows.standfirst: House speaker Matt Ritter said a $300 million buffer could bolster underfunded programs. Gov. Ned Lamont and Republicans don’t agree.

rows.title: What is CT’s Baby Bonds program? Here’s what to know
rows.standfirst: CT’s Baby Bonds program is a first-of-its kind statewide policy that would set aside funds for kids born into poverty to access as adults.

rows.title: CT must reform its pension investments now, Republicans say
rows.standfirst: A recent analysis from Yale concluded that poor pension fund investments have cost CT tens of billions of dollars over the past decade.

rows.title: Connecticut leaders tout ‘turnaround’ at investors conference
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont, Treasurer Erick Russell and lawmakers pitched Connecticut’s born-again faith in fiscal discipline to investors Tuesday

rows.title: CT union calls group home strike while pay demands look unlikely
rows.standfirst: SEIU 1199 went on strike at CT group homes hours before politicians urged the industry to brace for a funding hike short of its demands.

rows.title: A CT budget crisis is ‘on the horizon,’ legislators warn
rows.standfirst: With just over a week to go before CT’s legislative session ends, some say the state’s spending cap is setting up the next budget to fail.

rows.title: CT budget vote likely to run into final week of legislative session
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers are unlikely to vote on CT budget before next week, but leaders remain optimistic a bipartisan deal will be enacted by June 7.
